title: Who owns ‘brain rot’? Inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
key_facts: Tung Tung Tung Sahur, an AI-generated "Italian brain rot" character, was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teen using the username Noxa, with OpenAI's image tool.
French agency Mementum represents Noxa; two companies behind the Roblox game "Steal a Brainrot" sued Mementum in a US federal court in northern California.
The game's owners argue AI-generated work cannot be copyrighted because US law requires human authorship.
Court documents in a separate French dispute show the character took 15 minutes and seven prompts.
A 2025 US Copyright Office report says purely AI-generated material is not protected, and that mixed cases are judged one by one.
Mementum used an EU Digital Services Act takedown to remove the character from the game, then countersued for trademark infringement; it holds no US trademark yet.
A Cornell law professor said the case could yield a clear ruling on what is copyrightable when AI is involved.
quote_evidence: "Mementum's claimed rights do not exist. Under established law, copyright protection requires human authorship, and AI-generated material does not qualify."
"We are not claiming in this case that AI-assisted work can never be owned by anybody," said Aaron Moss
The copyright office's report does not offer a clear standard for ownership of creations that involve AI
why_it_matters_hint: Could clarify who owns characters made with a few AI prompts.
